lines.text: Look closely at your skin. Those tiny dots… are pores.
The pores you can see are little doorways, into narrow tunnels called hair follicles.
Even where you can't see one… a fine hair is usually growing inside.
Partway down sits a small oil gland. Its cells do something strange.
Each one slowly fills with oil… until the whole cell breaks down and becomes oil.
That oil is called sebum. It glides up along the hair, and spreads over your skin in a thin, soft coat.
Tiny microbes live in there too, quietly feeding on that oil.
That's a pore. A doorway. A hair. A gland. And its tiny residents.
